focus: Busan Political Crisis: domestic martial-law instruments, Won Yong-deok execution account, and personnel/security chain

material_findings.finding: A Korean contemporaneous record materially corrects the pass272 formulation that the Korean martial-law decree/appointment chain was still wholly pending. Defense Minister Shin Tae-young's May 24 statement says emergency martial law would take effect at 00:00 May 25, names Army Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Lee Jong-chan as martial-law commander, and separately appoints Maj. Gen. Won Yong-deok as Southern District martial-law commander responsible for the listed Gyeongsangnam-do districts including Pusan.

The same Korean record states the public rationale as renewed guerrilla activity and rear-area security after martial law had been broadly lifted for local elections. This is the government's stated rationale and must be modeled separately from the US Embassy's contemporaneous assessment that the Pusan inclusion was politically motivated.

Won Yong-deok's May 27 public statement supplies a Korean execution-side account of the May 26 National Assembly bus detention. Won said the bus failed to comply with a checkpoint at the temporary central government building, was towed to the 70th Military Police unit, occupants initially withheld identities, a roster was later made, the identities were reported upward, and after instructions they were allowed to act freely. This establishes a claimed reporting/instruction chain but does not identify who issued the decisive superior instruction.

Won's statement also repeats the official security rationale, citing guerrilla activity, alleged red-cell agitation in Pusan, and Pusan's logistics-base importance. Because this is the martial-law commander's own public defense, it is evidence of the government's stated justification, not independent proof that those conditions necessitated the Pusan political measures.

A May 24 Korean report confirms Yi Pom-sok was appointed State Council member and Home Minister replacing Chang Sok-yun on the eve of martial law. FRUS editorial reconstruction additionally identifies Hong Pom-hui as Vice Home Minister and Yun-Kyong as Chief of National Police immediately before proclamation. These appointments create a separate police/interior personnel branch that must not be collapsed into the Army martial-law chain.

FRUS editorial note identifies So Min-ho's May 25 arrest as the government's first act under martial law and says military police then attempted arrests of opposition assemblymen. This makes So's arrest and the later Assembly-bus detention distinct sub-events requiring distinct order attribution.

The National Assembly's May 28 resolution demanding termination of Pusan martial law passed 96-3 with 139 present. Debate by Kwak Sang-hoon explicitly invoked the detention of more than forty legislators' vehicle. This domestic legislative response independently contradicts any model in which the bus incident was institutionally treated as a routine checkpoint episode.

US contingency planning later contemplated an order to General Lee and the Second Logistic Command for protective surveillance, while explicitly preferring police/security control over UNC martial law. This reinforces that Lee Jong-chan's role must be separated across Korean legal command, UNC operational control, and hypothetical US/UNC protective measures.

adversarial_checks: The Korean May 24 announcement was sought specifically to challenge the earlier FRUS-only reconstruction of command appointments.
The government's security rationale is preserved verbatim in substance but not upgraded into an independently verified necessity finding.
The US Embassy's political-motive assessment is retained as a contemporaneous institutional assessment, not an omniscient fact statement.
Won's May 27 bus account is treated as a party/executor account and checked against the Assembly's contrary institutional reaction.
The bus detention is not merged with So Min-ho's arrest or other legislator arrests because the mechanisms and dates differ.
The phrase 'reported upward and released on instruction' is not used to infer the identity of the superior without the missing order/log.
Lee Jong-chan being named overall martial-law commander is not treated as proof he ordered the May 26 bus detention.
Won's appointment is now domestically corroborated, but the exact underlying legal instrument/order number remains a lead.
Interior/police appointments are modeled separately from Army martial-law appointments.
FRUS romanization 'Yun-Kyong' is not silently converted into a guessed Korean identity; the actor remains identity-unresolved.
Hong Pom-hui's identity is not merged with similarly named political figures until a Korean appointment record is recovered.
US/UNC contingency plans involving General Lee are kept hypothetical unless evidence shows implementation.
